chemistry-e1-l1.title: Di different properties of objects and materials · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-e1-l1.concept: Wetin dey make things na material. Metal, plastic, glass and rubber each get dia own special properties.
chemistry-e1-l1.example: Dem dey make window with clear glass wey light fit pass well, and dem dey make tyre with rubber wey stretch well and strong.

chemistry-e1-l2.title: Di different properties of objects and materials · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-e1-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about di different properties of objects and materials.
chemistry-e1-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-e2-l1.title: Materials wey dissolve for water and mixtures · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-e2-l1.concept: If one material dissolve well inside liquid until you no fit see am again, dem dey call am 'dissolving'. Materials wey no dissolve dey sink to di bottom or float.
chemistry-e2-l1.example: Salt dey dissolve clear inside water, but sand no dey dissolve inside water and e dey sink to di bottom.

chemistry-e2-l2.title: Materials wey dissolve for water and mixtures · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-e2-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about materials wey dissolve for water and mixtures.
chemistry-e2-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-e3-l1.title: Di three states: solid, liquid, gas · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-e3-l1.concept: Solid get fixed shape and volume. Liquid dey change shape according to di container but di volume dey fixed. Gas dey change both shape and volume freely.
chemistry-e3-l1.example: Ice (solid), water (liquid) and water vapor (gas) na di three states of water.

chemistry-e3-l2.title: Di three states: solid, liquid, gas · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-e3-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about di three states: solid, liquid, gas.
chemistry-e3-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-e4-l1.title: Evaporation, boiling, condensation and volume change of ice · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-e4-l1.concept: Liquid turning gas na vaporization (evaporation, boiling), gas turning liquid na liquefaction (condensation), and solid turning liquid na melting.
chemistry-e4-l1.example: For cold winter, wen water freeze di volume dey increase so drink cans and plastic bottles dey swell.

chemistry-e4-l2.title: Evaporation, boiling, condensation and volume change of ice · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-e4-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about evaporation, boiling, condensation and volume change of ice.
chemistry-e4-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-e5-l1.title: Solute, solvent, solution and concentration · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-e5-l1.concept: Di material wey dey dissolve na solute, di liquid wey dey dissolve am na solvent, and di liquid wey dem mix well na solution. For solution, di taste, colour and concentration dey di same for any part wey you scoop.
chemistry-e5-l1.example: If you dissolve salt (solute) inside water (solvent), e become salt water (solution).

chemistry-e5-l2.title: Solute, solvent, solution and concentration · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-e5-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about solute, solvent, solution and concentration.
chemistry-e5-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-e6-l1.title: Acidity, basicity and di 3 elements of combustion · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-e6-l1.concept: Acidic solutions (vinegar, lemon juice) dey turn blue litmus paper red, and basic solutions (soapy water) dey turn red paper blue. Combustion need fuel, oxygen, and temperature above di ignition point.
chemistry-e6-l1.example: If you put vinegar inside red cabbage indicator e turn red, and if you put soapy water e turn blue or yellow.

chemistry-e6-l2.title: Acidity, basicity and di 3 elements of combustion · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-e6-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about acidity, basicity and di 3 elements of combustion.
chemistry-e6-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-m1-l1.title: Boyle's law, Charles's law and change of state · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-m1-l1.concept: If temperature constant, gas volume dey inversely proportional to pressure (Boyle's law: $PV=\text{constant}$). If pressure constant, gas volume dey proportional to temperature (Charles's law).
chemistry-m1-l1.example: If you put dented ping-pong ball inside hot water, di gas particles go move more active and di ball go straighten tight.

chemistry-m1-l2.title: Boyle's law, Charles's law and change of state · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-m1-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about boyle's law, Charles's law and change of state.
chemistry-m1-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-m2-l1.title: Elements, atoms, ions and precipitation reactions · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-m2-l1.concept: Element na di basic component wey make up matter. If atom lose electrons e become positive ion, and if e gain electrons e become negative ion. If some ions meet, dem dey form precipitate wey no dissolve for water.
chemistry-m2-l1.example: If you put silver nitrate solution inside sodium chloride solution, white silver chloride ($\text{AgCl}$) precipitate go form.

chemistry-m2-l2.title: Elements, atoms, ions and precipitation reactions · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-m2-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about elements, atoms, ions and precipitation reactions.
chemistry-m2-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-m3-l1.title: Conservation of mass, constant composition, exothermic and endothermic · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-m3-l1.concept: Before and after chemical reaction, di type and number of atoms no dey change, so di total mass dey conserved. For compound, di mass ratio between di component elements dey fixed.
chemistry-m3-l1.example: Hydrogen $1\text{ g}$ and oxygen $8\text{ g}$ combine to make water $9\text{ g}$ (mass ratio $1:8$).

chemistry-m3-l2.title: Conservation of mass, constant composition, exothermic and endothermic · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-m3-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about conservation of mass, constant composition, exothermic and endothermic.
chemistry-m3-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-h1-l1.title: Ionic bond, covalent bond and oxidation-reduction · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-h1-l1.concept: Elements dey form ionic bonds or covalent bonds to satisfy di octet rule (Group 18 electron configuration). Oxidation na losing electrons, and reduction na gaining electrons.
chemistry-h1-l1.example: Sodium chloride ($\text{NaCl}$) no dey conduct electricity wen e be solid, but if you dissolve am inside water, di ions dey move and current dey flow.

chemistry-h1-l2.title: Ionic bond, covalent bond and oxidation-reduction · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-h1-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about ionic bond, covalent bond and oxidation-reduction.
chemistry-h1-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-h2-l1.title: Mole (mol) and quantitative relationships for chemical equations · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-h2-l1.concept: $6.02 \times 10^{23}$ particles dem dey call am $1\text{ mol}$. Di coefficient ratio of chemical equation equal to mole ratio, molecule number ratio, and volume ratio of gases.
chemistry-h2-l1.example: Di volume of gas $1\text{ mol}$ (for $0^\circ\text{C}$, $1\text{atm}$) na $22.4\text{ L}$.

chemistry-h2-l2.title: Mole (mol) and quantitative relationships for chemical equations · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-h2-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about mole (mol) and quantitative relationships for chemical equations.
chemistry-h2-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-h3-l1.title: Reaction rate, Le Chatelier's principle and chemical cells · Basic study and core principles
chemistry-h3-l1.concept: Catalyst dey control di rate by changing di activation energy. If you disturb dynamic equilibrium system, di equilibrium go shift for di direction wey dey reduce dat change (Le Chatelier's principle).
chemistry-h3-l1.example: Wen dem dey synthesize ammonia with di Haber-Bosch process, if dem increase di pressure, di equilibrium go shift to di forward reaction wey dey reduce di number of gas molecules.

chemistry-h3-l2.title: Reaction rate, Le Chatelier's principle and chemical cells · Experiment analysis and problem solving
chemistry-h3-l2.concept: Dis lesson dey build di ability to interpret experimental data and solve problems for real life about reaction rate, Le Chatelier's principle and chemical cells.
chemistry-h3-l2.example: E dey draw scientific conclusions through quantitative data analysis and error analysis.

chemistry-e1-q1.prompt: Wetin dey among dese ones na correct match of 'object' (thing wey get specific shape and use) and 'material' (di stuff wey dem take make am)?

options.a: Chair (object) — wood (material)
options.b: Glass (object) — cup (material)
options.c: Metal (object) — scissors (material)
options.d: Plastic (object) — bowl (material)

hints: 'Object' na di name of di finished thing wey we dey use, 'material' na di name of di stuff wey dem take make am.
Chair na thing, wood na di material.
chemistry-e1-q1.explanation: Thing wey get shape and use dem dey call am 'object', and di basic stuff wey dem take make di object dem dey call am 'material'.

chemistry-e1-q2.prompt: Wetin be di special property of material wey, if you pull am e go stretch, and wen you leave am e go return to im original shape, like rubber band or balloon?

options.a: Elasticity
options.b: Transparency
options.c: Magnetism
options.d: Flammability

hints: Na di property wey dey make something spring back to im original shape.
Think about di stretch wey you feel for rubber band.
chemistry-e1-q2.explanation: Di property wey dey make object wey force don change im shape return to im original shape wen di force don go, dem dey call am 'elasticity'.

chemistry-e1-q3.prompt: Which pair correctly match di properties of di materials wey dem take make 'raincoat' wey people dey wear wen rain dey fall and 'swimming goggles' wey people dey use for water play?

options.a: Raincoat: waterproof, e no dey allow water pass / Goggles: transparent, you fit see well
options.b: Raincoat: conductive, e dey carry electricity well / Goggles: brittle, e dey break easily
options.c: Raincoat: flammable, e dey burn well / Goggles: heavy
options.d: Raincoat: absorbent, e dey soak water well / Goggles: opaque

hints: Raincoat no suppose let water enter, and goggles must let you see front clear.
Di use of thing dey follow di property of di material.
chemistry-e1-q3.explanation: Dem dey make raincoat with waterproof material (vinyl/plastic) wey dey push water comot so rain no go wet you, and dem dey make swimming goggles with transparent plastic or glass so you fit see inside water.

chemistry-e1-q4.prompt: Wetin be di science reason why dem dey make di body of frying pan or pot for kitchen with metal, but dem dey make di handle with plastic or wood?

options.a: Because metal dey carry heat fast, but plastic and wood no dey carry heat well, so hand no go burn
options.b: Because metal handle too light
options.c: Because plastic dey change di taste of food make e sweet
options.d: So dem go fit make hole for di pot body

hints: To cook food, heat must reach di bottom of di pot quick.
You no fit hold handle wey hot.
chemistry-e1-q4.explanation: Metal dey conduct heat well so e dey cook food fast, and plastic and wood dey block heat well, so you fit hold di handle wen you dey cook without say fire burn you.

chemistry-e1-c.prompt: [Advanced environment study] Plastic light, strong and e no dey rot, but wen dem throw am away e no dey break down for nature for hundreds of years, so e dey pollute di environment. Which one na correct direction for material science to solve dis wahala?

options.a: To develop 'biodegradable plastic' wey dem make from corn starch and so on, wey microbes fit break down for nature
options.b: To throw all di plastic inside sea make e sink
options.c: To bury plastic deep inside ground and forget about am
options.d: To change all household things to single-use only

hints: Na new eco-friendly material wey dey friendly to nature and wey microbes fit chop and break down.
Na biodegradable technology.
chemistry-e1-c.explanation: To reduce environmental pollution, people dey develop biodegradable bio-plastic wey dem make from plant materials, and wey microbes go break down to water and carbon dioxide after some time.

chemistry-e1-q5.prompt: If iron nail or scissors stay for water and air for long time, e go rust and turn red. Which one na correct material science way to stop dis?

options.a: Rub thin layer of oil or paint am so air and water no go touch am
options.b: Soak am inside water to remove di air
options.c: Wash di iron with salt water every day
options.d: Dry am well for sun and keep am hotter

hints: For iron to corrode (oxidize), e need both oxygen and water.
If you coat di surface, e fit block oxygen and water.
chemistry-e1-q5.explanation: Iron dey corrode through di interaction of oxygen and water, so if you rub oil, paint, or plate di surface so air and water no touch am at all, e no go rust.

chemistry-e2-q1.prompt: If you put one spoon of sugar inside beaker wey get warm water and stir am with glass rod, which statement about wetin go happen na correct?

options.a: Di sugar grains break into very tiny pieces and spread well inside all di water until you no fit see dem again
options.b: Di sugar turn hard like stone for di bottom of di beaker
options.c: Di sugar rise above di water and fly commot inside air
options.d: Di water inside di beaker turn black

hints: Look di dissolving (melting inside water) wey dey happen.
E go clear, but if you taste am e still go sweet.
chemistry-e2-q1.explanation: Wen sugar dissolve inside water, di sugar molecules spread well between di water molecules until you no fit see dem again, and e turn clear sugar water.

chemistry-e2-q2.prompt: Why sugar dey dissolve pass for cup of warm water than for cup of cold water?

options.a: Because di hotter di temperature, di more di water molecules dey move, and dem dey pull di sugar grains comot quick
options.b: Because warm water dey cool di sugar down
options.c: Because warm water get more air inside
options.d: Because cold water dey push sugar away

hints: Di hotter e be, di faster di molecules dey move.
Think about wen you put sugar cube inside tea cup and stir am.
chemistry-e2-q2.explanation: Di hotter di water, di more active di heat motion of di water molecules, so dem dey hit di sugar particles more often and harder, and di dissolving speed go increase.

chemistry-e2-q3.prompt: If you pour salt water and muddy water separately inside funnel wey get filter paper, which pair correctly show wetin remain on top di filter paper?

options.a: Salt water: nothing remain / Muddy water: soil grains remain on di filter paper
options.b: Salt water: lump of salt remain / Muddy water: nothing remain
options.c: Both salt water and muddy water pass through di filter paper as e be
options.d: Both salt water and muddy water remain on top di filter paper

hints: Di particles for solution wey don dissolve well small pass di holes for filter paper.
Soil grains wey no dissolve go dey caught by di filter paper.
chemistry-e2-q3.explanation: Salt don dissolve completely so im particles small pass di gaps for filter paper and dem all pass through, but soil grains no dissolve so dem no fit pass di holes and dem remain.

chemistry-e2-q4.prompt: To get clean salt wey we dey chop from sea water, which change of state and separation method dem dey use for salt farm?

options.a: Use sun and wind make di water for sea water evaporate and leave only di salt crystals
options.b: Boil di sea water hard until e turn ice
options.c: Put magnet inside sea water to pull di salt
options.d: Use sieve to filter di salt comot from sea water

hints: Wen sea water wey dem spread shallow for salt farm collect sun, only di water dey turn water vapor and fly go.
Na separation of mixture by evaporation.
chemistry-e2-q4.explanation: If dem keep sea water for salt farm and use sun and wind make di water evaporate, only di water go turn water vapor (gas) and fly go, and only di white salt crystals wey dissolve before go remain.

chemistry-e2-c.prompt: [Advanced principle study] Dem dissolve 10 g of salt completely inside 100 g of water to make salt water. If you weigh all di salt water with electronic scale, how many g e go be?
hints: Even if di salt dissolve until you no fit see am again, e no vanish.
Conservation of mass: (weight of water) + (weight of salt) = ?
chemistry-e2-c.explanation: Wen something dissolve, di particles of di solute (salt) just spread between di water molecules, dem no vanish, so di total weight of di solution na di sum of di weight of water and salt, wey be 110 g exactly.

chemistry-e2-q5.prompt: Why water and cooking oil dey separate again into two layers after small time, even if you put dem inside one bottle and shake am well well?

options.a: Because cooking oil no dey mix with water and e lighter (less dense) than water so e dey float for top
options.b: Because cooking oil dey absorb di water
options.c: Because di water warm pass di cooking oil
options.d: Because di cooking oil don turn solid

hints: Water dey polar and oil dey non-polar, so dem no dey dissolve each other.
Oil lighter than water (less dense) so e dey float for top.
chemistry-e2-q5.explanation: Water na polar molecule and cooking oil na non-polar molecule, so dem no dey mix, and di density of cooking oil (about 0.92 g/cm³) small pass water (1.0 g/cm³), so e dey float to di top layer.

chemistry-e3-q1.prompt: Which state of matter dey change shape freely according to di container wey you put am inside, but di volume no dey change and e dey stay di same?

options.a: Liquid
options.b: Solid
options.c: Gas
options.d: Plasma

hints: Think about wen you dey pour water or milk go another cup.
Di shape dey follow di cup, but di quantity (volume) remain di same.
chemistry-e3-q1.explanation: For liquid, di bonds between molecules dey more flexible pass for solid, so di shape dey change easy according to di container, but di attraction between molecules still dey, so di volume dey constant.

chemistry-e3-q2.prompt: Dem fill one syringe with water and another with air, then dem block di mouth with finger and push di piston hard. Wetin go happen?

options.a: Di piston for di syringe wey get air go push in well, but di one wey get water almost no go move
options.b: Di syringe wey get water go push in pass di one wey get air
options.c: Both syringes go push in completely to di end
options.d: Neither of di two syringes go move at all

hints: Gas molecules dey far from each other so plenty empty space dey.
Gas dey compress well, but liquid very hard to compress.
chemistry-e3-q2.explanation: For gas (air), di distance between molecules too far, so if you apply pressure e go compress easy and di volume go reduce, but for liquid (water), di molecules don already pack tight so e almost no dey compress.

chemistry-e3-q3.prompt: Which one na common feature of 'solid' materials wey we dey see around us?

options.a: Di shape and volume dey remain di same even if dem change di container
options.b: Di shape dey change freely according to di container
options.c: You no fit hold am with hand and you no fit see am at all
options.d: E dey fill all di space and spread without end

hints: Think about wen you move wood or stone from one box go another.
Di shape no dey change.
chemistry-e3-q3.explanation: For solid, di particles wey make di material dey bond tight and regular, so di shape and volume dey remain di same unless outside force dey act on am.

chemistry-e3-q4.prompt: Dem open perfume bottle for one corner of room, and after small time, person for di other side of di room smell di sweet scent for im nose. Wetin be di science principle wey explain dis?

options.a: Di perfume gas particles dey move by demsef and spread inside air, wey dem dey call 'diffusion'
options.b: Because di perfume liquid freeze and roll for floor
options.c: Because di perfume molecules pull di nose like magnet
options.d: Because di air chop di perfume smell

hints: Di particles wey make matter no dey rest, dem dey always move by demsef.
Wetin dem dey call di way gas dey spread?
chemistry-e3-q4.explanation: Di way perfume particles dey always move freely by demsef for all direction inside air and spread from where e plenty to where e small, na im dem dey call 'diffusion'.

chemistry-e3-c.prompt: [Advanced thought experiment] Air wey we no fit see, e get weight (mass) like solid or liquid? Which experiment method dey most reasonable to prove am?

options.a: Weigh basketball wey dem fill with air with precise electronic scale, then remove di air and weigh am again to check di weight difference
options.b: Throw balloon up high and watch how e dey fly
options.c: Put empty glass bottle for sun and check if e dey warm
options.d: Put hand inside water and measure how cold di water be

hints: Gas na matter too, so e get mass.
Compare di scale reading wen air dey inside and wen dem remove am.
chemistry-e3-c.explanation: If you measure di weight of ball wey full with air and then remove di air and measure again, you go see say di weight don reduce, and dis prove say air, wey be gas, get mass and weight.

chemistry-e3-q5.prompt: Wen dem put cold 'dry ice' wey dem dey use pack ice cream for room temperature, no liquid water drop dey form at all, e just turn gas straight and fly go. Wetin be dis change of state?

options.a: 'Sublimation', where solid turn gas straight without passing through liquid
options.b: 'Melting', where solid melt into liquid
options.c: 'Vaporization', where liquid boil into gas
options.d: 'Condensation', where gas turn liquid

hints: Dry ice na solid carbon dioxide.
For 1 atm and room temperature, e dey sublime go gas directly without passing through liquid state.
chemistry-e3-q5.explanation: Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) no fit exist as liquid for normal pressure (1 atm), so e dey show 'sublimation', where e dey change from solid go gas straight.

chemistry-e4-q1.prompt: Dem take cold drink can comot from fridge just now and put am for table for small time, and small water drops form for di surface of di can. Where dis water drops come from?

options.a: Water vapor (gas) wey dey inside air touch di cold can and condense into liquid water
options.b: Di drink leak comot through di aluminium wall of di can
options.c: Water drops wey form from paint for di can surface wey melt
options.d: Sap wey comot from di wood for di table

hints: Water vapor wey you no fit see dey always float inside air.
Wen water vapor meet cold surface e cool down and turn liquid water drops (condensation).
chemistry-e4-q1.explanation: Na 'condensation (liquefaction)' be dis: di water vapor wey dey gas state inside air meet di cold can surface, lose heat, and turn liquid water drops.
